title: Privacy settings, rights requests, retention and compliance checker

changes.description: Settings → DPDP & Privacy. It holds the privacy contact, request periods, notices and breach templates (versioned, published only when complete), consent purposes, data collection, retention rules, children, links, breach contacts, processors and owner attestations. Values the law fixes are locked.
A DPDP compliance checker in Settings and CI. It shows a score for each check, when the check last passed and how to fix it, and offers a counts-only report download.
The candidate portal opens with the privacy notice. Optional consents are separate and unticked, and candidates can make a rights request from the portal.
My Privacy, for every staff member: their data summary, processors, consents (with one-click withdrawal), rights requests and nomination.

Privacy cases, for Super Admin and PnC Admin: a rights request queue with due dates and escalation, an incident register with live CERT-In and Board countdowns and drafted messages, legal holds, and guardian consent for joiners under 18.
A nightly retention job, dry run by default. It never deletes anything under a year old, skips anything under a legal hold, and writes a counts-only report.
Closing a confirmation review seals its peer feedback into the vault.
The email outbox shows each message's template with sample values in place of a stored body.
Candidate personal-details fields start empty.
Identity and bank documents are never copied to Drive.
Server functions run in the Mumbai region.
The audit, activity, settings-change and email logs are written by the server only.
Email logs keep no message bodies.
Audit descriptions carry no reasons or amounts.

title: RBAC v1 roles, the core/vault split, and record sealing

changes.description: Replaced the ten display-name roles with the RBAC v1 twelve-role model; rank now controls impersonation only, and only within a group, so a PnC Admin cannot become a Fin Ops to reach bank details.

Role grants defer to a single authority and use the caller's real role, so impersonating a Super Admin no longer grants like one; Platform Admin can never widen sight of sensitive data, for others or itself.
Fixed current_app_role, can_manage_forms and the enforce-owner trigger, which hardcoded the old role names — can_manage_forms guards ten RLS policies that would all have started denying.
Document numbers are stored in the vault; core keeps only the last four characters, and the full number is readable solely through a logged function that refuses Exec View.
Added the vault project schema, with an append-only access log, service-role-only RLS, and its own role table that refuses core-only roles.

Added sealing — verified documents and closed-cycle feedback move to the vault and leave a completion marker behind, with the database refusing to call a record sealed while the file or text is still in core.
Added withdrawal, which keeps the record so no confirmation trigger can fire for someone who never joined, and surfaces their unsealed documents as orphaned exposures.
The role picker and role switcher now offer only what the caller may actually grant or impersonate, instead of static lists the server silently refused.
Removed `email.includes("admin")` as a privilege check in two places.

title: Candidate-to-Employee Pipeline: Auth, Persistence, Documents, Letters and Annexure

changes.description: Added middleware.ts gating every route behind a verified Supabase session. getCurrentUserRole previously returned Super Admin whenever no user was signed in, and no middleware or layout redirect existed, so every dashboard route and server action was open to anonymous visitors.

Enforced canAccessRoute server-side for pages and API routes, matched longest-prefix so /manage/letter-templates, /manage/letters, /manage/signatories and /manage/onboarding stay with the onboarding feature rather than being gated as manage-users.

Candidate documents are stored in a private Supabase Storage bucket and served only through 10-minute signed URLs; employee document links now redirect through a route that signs a fresh URL per click.
Cron routes fail closed when CRON_SECRET is unset, instead of accepting the literal header "Bearer undefined".

Onboarding now persists. The service kept state in a process-local Map and its only Supabase insert minted ids like onb-<timestamp> against a uuid column, so it always failed silently; a candidate could complete the entire portal and have nothing survive the request.
Removed the demo-seed fallback that made an empty onboarding table display five fabricated candidates.

Sending an invitation now actually emails the candidate. sendOnboardingInvitation flipped the status to invited and logged "invitation sent" without ever calling sendEmail. It now sends first and records second, and reports failures to P&C.
Candidate document upload collects a real file. The portal had no file input: handleMockUpload fabricated a filename and size per document type, so identity and bank proofs existed only as strings.
Provisioning creates the employees row. It previously logged "Employee Record Linked ... in the central NG workforce directory" and inserted nothing, so a completed onboarding produced no employee.
Corrected an employee_profiles write that used columns the table does not have, and added part_time and fellow to the employee_type enum, which employee_types seeds but the enum lacked.

Salary annexure: salary_structures and salary_rules derive the Basic / HRA / Special Allowance / Gross / Employer PF / CTC breakdown per employee type, rendered as Annexure A in the letters, the candidate portal and the P&C review screen.

One letter pipeline. Letters render from letter_templates into candidate_letters and are what the candidate signs; the hardcoded templates.ts offer and appointment letters were deleted. Adds employee agreement, acceptance letter and annexure document types, and persists the captured signature image and metadata, which previously had no columns.
Verified candidate documents are carried to the employee record on provisioning, with a best-effort Drive copy, and personal details are carried into employee_profiles.
The candidate document checklist is driven by document_types rather than five hardcoded strings, and adds photograph, professional references and previous experience/relieving letters.

Provisioning refuses while a required document is unverified, allocates sequential employee codes instead of random ones, and records credential delivery as pending because the application never stores an account password.
Portal submission is gated on what is outstanding and names the remaining items; record reads are batched one query per child table instead of one query per record.
